sentences.text: Accused No.3 in Crime No.427/2024 registered by Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471, 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., seeking anticipatory bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.427/2024 was registered by Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bengaluru, against one Hardeep D and others for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 29.10.2024 received from Hanamatraya T.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner herein who was arraigned as accused No.3 in the FIR had filed Crl.Misc.No.10110/2024 before jurisdictional Sessions Court which was rejected on 15.11.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that accused Nos.1 and 2 have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court NC: 2024:KHC:51318 in Crl.P.No.12721/2024.
The allegation made against all the accused are similar.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

6. A perusal of the averments found in the first information would reveal that petitioner is the owner of the property bearing Nos.6 and 7 situated at Mallathahalli Village, Ward No.129 within the limits of Rajarajeshwarinagar Range of BBMP and accused Nos.1 and 2, who are partners of a Company known as M/s.
Lak Ven Developers had allegedly constructed a multistoreyed building in the aforesaid property in violation of the sanction plan.
The allegations found in the first information as against accused Nos.1 and 2 and the petitioner herein are similar.
Accused Nos.1 and 2 have been granted bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.12721/2024.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that on the ground of parity, petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:-
Shri Lakshmi Prasad G vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131416348/
2 7.

sentences.text: The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.427/2024 NC:
2024:KHC:51318 registered by Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471, 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future;
